points.quote: Page mode and edgeless mode are two views of the same Yjs doc, which is one block tree. ... Switching mode only changes how that tree is rendered.
Its children are one `affine:surface` block and the `affine:note` blocks. ... The `affine:surface` block has one prop, `elements`.
These are "surface elements" and are not blocks. They include shape, brush (freehand drawing), connector, text, mindmap and group, and they are stored as plain data.
Notes hold the page-mode content (paragraphs, lists and so on). In edgeless mode they appear as movable cards.

Several block types are allowed as children of the surface block (`surface-model.ts`): `affine:frame`, `affine:image`, `affine:bookmark`, `affine:attachment`, `affine:embed-*` and `affine:edgeless-text`. Notes sit beside the surface, not under it.

Block-based items (notes, frames, images and the rest) are real child blocks. They carry the same `xywh` and `index` props as block props. ... the `xywh` prop holds a serialized string like `"[x,y,w,h]"`.

**Stacking order:** `index` is a fractional-index string such as `'a0'`. The string's lexical order is the z-order. ... Blocks and elements share one index space, so they can be layered against each other.

A `group` element has a `children` Y.Map of `childId → true`, plus a `title` Y.Text ... A `frame` is a block. It keeps `childElementIds: Record<id, boolean>` and its own `xywh` and `index` (`frame-model.ts`).
